If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and price is trending down, add 1–3% to forecast in mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward bias.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is above true value, subtract 1–4% in late horizon (16–30 days) to align with mean reversion.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 after a sharp drop, increase forecast by 3–6% in early horizon to capture momentum reversal.  
If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) across 5+ days, reduce forecast by 5–8% in late horizon to reflect subdued market sentiment.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and true price is below forecast, reduce forecast by 2–5% in mid horizon to avoid overcorrection.
